skill.name: creating-financial-models
skill.description: Provides guidance and Python helpers for DCF valuation, WACC, terminal value, equity value, sensitivity tables, scenario analysis, and breakeven analysis.
skill.summary: Build DCF valuations, sensitivity tests, and scenario analyses for investment decisions.
skill.author: anthropics

content.value_statement: Financial valuation requires consistent assumptions, risk tests, and clear outputs. This skill helps build DCF models, sensitivity tables, and scenario views for investment analysis.
actual_capabilities: Builds DCF projections from revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital, tax, growth, and margin assumptions.
Calculates WACC from CAPM inputs, debt cost, tax rate, and capital structure.
Computes enterprise value using perpetuity growth or exit multiple terminal value methods.
Derives equity value and value per share from enterprise value, net debt, cash, and share count.
Creates one-way, two-way, tornado, scenario, breakeven, and Excel-style sensitivity tables.
Generates text valuation summaries and helper metrics such as beta and free cash flow CAGR.
limitations: The Python scripts do not fetch market data or financial statements automatically.
Monte Carlo simulation is described in the guide, but no dedicated Monte Carlo script is included.
Models depend on user-provided assumptions and may not reflect current market conditions.
The skill is not a substitute for licensed investment, tax, or legal advice.

use_cases.title: Value a Public Company
use_cases.description: Build a five-year DCF model, calculate WACC, and estimate enterprise and equity value from provided financials.

use_cases.title: Test Fundraising Assumptions
use_cases.description: Compare growth, margin, and cash flow assumptions before presenting a financing plan to stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Compare Acquisition Scenarios
use_cases.description: Model base, upside, and downside cases with probability weights and sensitivity tables for deal review.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic DCF
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner valuation from supplied company financials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a DCF model for this company using the attached historical revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital, tax, debt, cash, and share count data. Show the key assumptions, enterprise value, equity value, and value per share.

prompt_templates.title: Run Sensitivity Tables
prompt_templates.prompt: Create one-way and two-way sensitivity tables for this valuation. Test WACC, terminal growth, EBITDA margin, and revenue growth ranges, then identify the strongest value drivers.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Weighted Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Build base, upside, and downside scenarios for this project. Apply the provided probability weights, calculate expected value, and summarize the assumptions that explain each outcome.

prompt_templates.title: Stress Test an Acquisition Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the supplied acquisition assumptions to build a DCF and equity value view. Add sensitivity tables, breakeven analysis, scenario probabilities, and a concise investment risk summary.

output_examples.input: A five-year DCF request for a mature software company with revenue, EBITDA, capex, working capital, and WACC inputs.
output_examples.output: A valuation summary with projected free cash flow, terminal value, enterprise value, equity value, and value per share.

output_examples.input: A request to test WACC and terminal growth ranges around a base valuation.
output: A two-way sensitivity table showing valuation outcomes across the selected ranges.
A short driver summary explaining which assumptions move value the most.

output_examples.input: A project finance request with base, upside, and downside assumptions plus probability weights.
output_examples.output: A scenario comparison with weighted expected value, case-level outputs, and key assumption notes.

best_practices: Separate inputs, calculations, outputs, and document each key assumption.
Cross-check valuation with multiple terminal value methods and sensitivity ranges.
Use current source data and review results with qualified finance professionals.
anti_patterns: Treating default assumptions as market facts.
Using a single valuation point without sensitivity or scenario checks.
Presenting model outputs as financial advice or guaranteed returns.

faq.question: Can it create a full DCF model?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure projections, WACC, terminal value, enterprise value, equity value, and valuation summaries from supplied assumptions.

faq.question: Does it connect to live market data?
faq.answer: No. Users must provide financial statements, market inputs, comparables, and current assumptions.

faq.question: Can it run Monte Carlo simulations?
faq.answer: The guide describes Monte Carlo analysis, but the included Python scripts focus on DCF and sensitivity workflows.

faq.question: What inputs are needed?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include historical financials, growth rates, margins, tax rate, capex, working capital, WACC components, debt, cash, and shares.

faq.question: Is this investment advice?
faq.answer: No. It supports financial modeling workflows and should be reviewed by qualified finance, tax, or legal professionals.

faq.question: Which AI tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
